purpose: Authoring blueprint for an independent, original Physics HL practice bank. Item ideas and pedagogy below are editorial recommendations, not IB questions or syllabus wording.
guideVersion: Published February 2023; corrected through November 2024; linked by official 2026 examiner instructions.
importantVersionFinding: The university-admission/subject-guides/physics-guide.pdf remains the initial uncorrected guide. Use the examiner-linked guide. Corrected details include thermal or radiation pressure in stellar equilibrium, the negative conduction gradient, mean-square molecular speed, and 50 marks for SL Paper 2.
scopeDigest: HL-only: A.4, A.5, B.4, D.4, E.2. Mixed: C.1, C.3, C.5, D.1, D.2, E.1, E.3. A.2 additionally permits 2D collision/explosion calculations at HL. Exclusions: resisted-projectile calculation; banked-track calculation; vertical-circle forces away from top/bottom; prescribed inertia memorization; centre-of-mass calculation; relativity derivations; AC circuit analysis; slit obliquity; pipe end corrections/pressure nodes; simultaneously moving source and observer; noncircular orbit calculation; quantitative self-induction/RL; Compton derivation; weak interaction; Cepheids. Constraints: rolling without slip; monatomic ideal gases; normal-incidence interference; monochromatic rectangular single slit; straight constant-speed worldlines with ct axis; radial gravity superposition along a two-body line; induction via perpendicular rods or rectangular coils. Added-HL targets: SHM phase/energy; single/multiple-slit/grating patterns; acoustic Doppler; gravitational/electric potential and energetics; nuclear size/scattering/Bohr; exponential decay/nuclear stability evidence. A clean data booklet accompanies all examinations.

topics.title: Kinematics
originalItemIdeas: Reconstruct a trolley journey from a signed velocity graph and distinguish displacement from distance.
Design a launch above or below horizontal where landing height differs; require separate vertical and horizontal reasoning.
Use frame-by-frame positions to decide whether acceleration is constant.
solutionPitfalls: Area under negative velocity counts negatively for displacement.
Do not use the same-height range expression for unequal launch and landing heights.

topics.title: Forces and momentum
originalItemIdeas: Predict whether a package slips on an accelerating platform using the static-friction inequality.
Combine buoyancy and viscous drag for a slowly falling sphere, explicitly stating the drag model.
Infer impulse from a force sensor trace; use a two-direction recoil problem for HL.
Compare support force at the top and bottom of a vertical loop.
solutionPitfalls: Centripetal force names the resultant radial force; it is not an additional force.
Third-law forces act on different objects.
Static friction is not always its limiting value.

topics.title: Work, energy and power
originalItemIdeas: Calculate useful energy and fuel use for a winch with measured losses.
Compare spring launch speeds using an energy argument, then evaluate a nonconservative correction.
Read work from a force-displacement plot.
solutionPitfalls: Use the force component parallel to motion.
Efficiency uses useful output over total input.
Mechanical energy can decrease while total energy remains conserved.

topics.title: Rigid body mechanics
originalItemIdeas: Move two masses along a rotating support and compare angular speed and rotational energy.
Give a wheel's inertia and model a constant-torque spin-up.
Compare two objects rolling down the same incline with their inertia formulae supplied.
Balance several forces about a pivot before a support is removed.
solutionPitfalls: Use perpendicular lever arms.
State the isolated system before conserving angular momentum.
Conservation of angular momentum does not imply conservation of rotational kinetic energy.

topics.title: Galilean and special relativity
originalItemIdeas: Transform two events and test whether their order or simultaneity changes.
Compare a classical velocity sum with a relativistic sum for a fast probe.
Use a travelling particle's lifetime to reconcile distance and time in two frames.
Extract a speed from a worldline and check the invariant interval.
diagramAssets: ct-x spacetime diagram with light lines
solutionPitfalls: Identify the frame in which events occur at the same position before calling an interval proper time.
Length must be measured simultaneously in its measuring frame.
Do not read transformed axes as ordinary equal-scale perpendicular axes.

topics.title: Thermal energy transfers
originalItemIdeas: Infer heat capacity and latent heat from a heater's temperature-time record.
Compare insulation slabs from a steady conduction experiment.
Use a star's spectrum and received flux to infer physical properties.
solutionPitfalls: Use kelvin in radiation laws; temperature differences can use kelvin or Celsius increments.
Separate net radiation from emission alone.
Use the signed temperature gradient only with a declared positive direction.

topics.title: Greenhouse effect
originalItemIdeas: Construct a one-layer planetary energy budget with explicitly defined absorption fractions.
Compare equilibrium temperatures after an albedo change.
Explain how molecular absorption and re-emission alter outgoing infrared transfer.
solutionPitfalls: The intercepted area is pi R squared and the emitting spherical area is four pi R squared.
Do not describe infrared as permanently trapped or confuse albedo with emissivity.

topics.title: Gas laws
originalItemIdeas: Determine gas amount from two measured states and test whether a leak occurred.
Connect a density change to molecular mean-square speed.
Evaluate when a dilute-gas model becomes unreliable.
solutionPitfalls: Distinguish mean speed, mean-square speed and rms speed.
Use absolute pressure and absolute temperature.
Apply monatomic internal-energy expressions only to the specified model.

topics.title: Thermodynamics
originalItemIdeas: Analyse a three-stage p-V cycle with simple area calculations and one adiabatic stage.
Compare a real engine's efficiency with its reservoir limit.
Calculate the total entropy change when heat transfers between two reservoirs.
Use a small coin model to distinguish a macrostate from its multiplicity.
solutionPitfalls: With Q = delta U + W, W is positive for expansion work done by the gas.
A complete cycle has zero net internal-energy change but can have nonzero work.
Local entropy can fall while the total rises.
For variable pressure use graph area; do not silently use one endpoint's pressure.

topics.title: Current and circuits
originalItemIdeas: Infer emf and internal resistance from terminal voltage against current.
Design an LDR or thermistor divider to cross a stated threshold.
Compare resistance and power when wire geometry changes.
Assess how a specified nonideal meter affects a reading.
solutionPitfalls: Identify parallel branches by common nodes, not visual placement.
Choose the correct axes before interpreting slope as resistance.
Distinguish emf from loaded terminal voltage.

topics.title: Simple harmonic motion
originalItemIdeas: Use acceleration versus displacement to identify SHM and determine period.
For HL, choose phase from initial displacement and velocity, then predict the next event.
For HL, partition energy at a specified fraction of amplitude.
solutionPitfalls: Check restoring direction, not merely proportional acceleration.
A speed expression has two possible velocity directions.
Use radians in phase calculations.

topics.title: Wave model
originalItemIdeas: Combine a spatial snapshot and a time trace to infer wave speed and particle motion.
Classify a disturbance by oscillation direction and need for a medium.
solutionPitfalls: A graph versus position gives wavelength; a graph versus time gives period.
Wave propagation and the oscillation of one particle are different motions.

topics.title: Wave phenomena
originalItemIdeas: Trace a ray through a boundary and test total internal reflection.
Predict interference from two sources with their phase relation explicitly specified.
For HL, vary slit width independently from slit separation and explain the combined pattern.
For HL, infer grating spacing and the largest observable order.
solutionPitfalls: Angles in Snell's law are measured from the normal.
Double-slit separation and individual slit width play different roles.
The single-slit central maximum has two first minima.
For an allowed grating order, the sine cannot exceed one.

topics.title: Standing waves and resonance
originalItemIdeas: Identify boundary conditions from two observed modes and predict the next allowed mode.
Compare phase of particles on either side of a node.
Match damping descriptions to amplitude-time and response-frequency curves.
solutionPitfalls: An open pipe end is a displacement antinode.
A fixed-free system has odd allowed harmonics.
Use first harmonic terminology and label displacement explicitly.

topics.title: Doppler effect
originalItemIdeas: Infer the radial recession speed of a source from a small spectral-line shift.
For HL, contrast approaching-source and approaching-observer sound calculations.
Use wavefront spacing to diagnose which object is moving.
solutionPitfalls: Declare whether a frequency or wavelength change is signed or a magnitude.
Approach must increase observed frequency.
Mechanical wave speed is measured relative to its medium.

topics.title: Gravitational fields
originalItemIdeas: Locate a zero-field point between unequal masses.
For HL, compare orbital energy before and after a circular-orbit change.
For HL, infer field strength from the local slope of a potential plot.
Explain a low-orbit satellite's speed change as atmospheric drag lowers its orbit.
solutionPitfalls: Radius is measured from the central body's centre.
Potential and potential energy remain negative when zero is at infinity.
Zero resultant field does not imply zero potential.
Include kinetic energy when comparing orbital states.

topics.title: Electric and magnetic fields
originalItemIdeas: Infer a charge quantum from a supplied set of droplet charges.
Compare conductor interior and exterior fields.
For HL, construct an equipotential map and infer the direction of force on each sign of charge.
For HL, sum potentials of several charges and evaluate the work in assembling a pair.
solutionPitfalls: Electric field follows the force on a positive test charge.
Potential is scalar; field is vector.
A conducting interior can have zero field but nonzero constant potential.

topics.title: Motion in electromagnetic fields
originalItemIdeas: Select undeflected particles using crossed fields, then infer charge-to-mass ratio from curvature.
Compare electric and magnetic deflection for particles with the same speed.
Determine the force direction and magnitude for parallel current-carrying wires.
solutionPitfalls: Magnetic force does no work on an isolated moving charge.
Reverse force direction for negative charge.
Specify field directions with clear dots/crosses and a legend.

topics.title: Induction
originalItemIdeas: Predict the signed emf pulse as a rectangular coil enters and leaves a finite field region.
Calculate a moving rod's emf and explain the required mechanical power under load.
Use a rotating coil's flux graph to infer emf phase and amplitude.
Explain the qualitative opposition to a changing current in a coil.
solutionPitfalls: Flux angle is measured to the area normal.
Only changing linked flux induces emf.
Lenz's law opposes the change, not necessarily the original field.

topics.title: Structure of the atom
originalItemIdeas: Match spectral lines to transitions in a newly supplied energy-level diagram.
For HL, compare nuclear radii and density across isotopes.
For HL, infer closest approach from projectile energy and discuss the fixed-target approximation.
For HL, connect allowed hydrogen energy levels to an ionization threshold.
solutionPitfalls: Photon energy equals the positive magnitude of an energy difference.
Use nuclear rather than atomic radius in scattering reasoning.
State when nuclear recoil is neglected.

topics.title: Quantum physics
originalItemIdeas: Infer Planck's constant and work function from a stopping-voltage graph.
Compare the separate effects of intensity and frequency on photoelectric measurements.
Predict matter-wave diffraction changes after an accelerating-voltage change.
Determine a Compton shift and explain the photon's energy loss.
solutionPitfalls: Below threshold, raising intensity does not cause single-photon photoemission.
Use maximum kinetic energy when relating to stopping voltage.
Compton angle is the photon scattering angle.

topics.title: Radioactive decay
originalItemIdeas: Balance a decay chain and identify the emitted lepton.
Extract half-life after background subtraction.
For HL, use a logarithmic activity plot to infer a decay constant and initial population.
Relate discrete and continuous radiation-energy spectra to conservation arguments.
solutionPitfalls: Subtract background before applying decay ratios.
Distinguish activity from detector count rate.
Keep atomic versus nuclear masses consistent.
For a finite interval, decay probability is 1 minus exp(-lambda t), not exactly lambda t.

topics.title: Fission
originalItemIdeas: Calculate energy per reaction from supplied masses, then estimate fuel consumption at a stated efficiency.
Explain how a changed neutron population affects a chain reaction.
Trace energy flow through a simplified reactor and distinguish component functions.
solutionPitfalls: A moderator slows neutrons; control rods absorb them.
Account for emitted neutrons in reaction balance.
Convert MeV to joules before power calculations.

topics.title: Fusion and stars
originalItemIdeas: Place stars from luminosity and temperature data on an HR diagram and compare radii.
Determine distance from parallax and connect it to observed brightness.
Calculate fusion energy from supplied masses and discuss the necessary conditions.
Compare the later evolution of two stars with explicitly stated initial masses.
diagramAssets: HR diagram with decreasing temperature to the right
solutionPitfalls: The support pressure can be thermal or radiative, depending on the star.
Large luminosity alone does not prove high surface temperature.
Parallax is the half-angle in the usual annual construction.

hlPaper1.paper1a: 40 MCQs, one mark each; no negative marking

ia.role: separate scientific investigation, not a question-bank exam paper

assessmentFacts.calculator: All current specimen papers require a calculator and clean data booklet; do not carry forward the old no-calculator Paper 1 rule.

recommendedBankDesign.status: Editorial recommendation, not an official exam prediction or topic weighting
recommendedBankDesign.coverageFloor: Each of the 24 subtopics should have at least two MCQs, one multi-part response, and a plotted/diagram-based item. Each mixed topic needs separate shared and AHL coverage. Give every theme at least two substantial data tasks.
recommendedBankDesign.markAllocationPrinciple: Choose the mark mix above when assembling exam practice; do not confuse the count of short MCQs with the count of long data tasks.
recommendedBankDesign.suggestedInitialScale: At least 144 independent question sets before claiming broad coverage, with expansion based on a knowledge-point coverage ledger. A set is one coherent stem and its parts, not each subpart counted separately.
recommendedBankDesign.themeShareRationale: A starting editorial allocation close to relative HL teaching time, not prescribed exam weighting.
recommendedBankDesign.reasoning: About half the marks in assembled practice should require analysis, evaluation or synthesis rather than recall and direct substitution. Use unfamiliar settings with all necessary contextual information supplied.
recommendedBankDesign.avoidLegacyCreep: Keep capacitance/RC, AC impedance, transformers, polarization, thin lenses, detailed particle classification, relativity energy-momentum and cosmological distance ladders outside core coverage unless explicitly supplied as unfamiliar context. Do not import old optional-topic modules.

dataTaskAuthoring.principle: Create fresh physical systems and independently calculated synthetic measurements. Label simulated data where appropriate; do not imply a real experiment occurred.
coverage: gradient uncertainty from extreme acceptable lines
a specific improvement tied to a specific limitation
constructionChecks: Generate values from a known physical model before adding bounded noise.
Keep the displayed precision consistent with the stated measurement resolution.
Provide enough points and range for the inference requested.
Keep at least one permissible best-fit/maximum/minimum line consistent with the error bars.
Do not force an intercept of zero when the model permits an offset.
Use fit-derived points for a gradient; specify a sensible acceptance interval.

markschemeDesign.officialConventionDigest: The specimen allocates integer marking points by subpart, accepts equivalent meaning and alternative methods, and permits error-carried-forward when specified. Marks have a stated maximum. Units or significant-figure errors are penalized only when a marking note requires it. Wording and grammar are not ends in themselves.
implementationAdvice: Store each marking point separately with its value, dependencies, accepted alternatives and any tolerance.
Keep the worked solution separate from the scoring rubric so a concise valid method is not rejected.
For a numerical result, show relation, substitution, result and unit, but allocate marks for the actual reasoning required.
For Explain, require a causal link; for Discuss, reward an evidenced comparison or qualified judgement.
For Show, use sufficient unrounded calculation to establish the target rather than reverse-substituting it.
For sketching, list the required intercepts, asymptotes, slope signs, axis labels and relative features.
MCQs need four distinct options with exactly one defensible best answer, plus explanations for distractors.
Include a common-error note that teaches the physics without changing the official-style credit rules.

diagramProduction.format: Original SVG or equivalent deterministic vector art, with text alternatives; never reuse exam artwork.
minimumStandards: All information needed to solve is visible in the stem or diagram.
Axes carry quantities and units; numerical plots use actual coordinates derived from the data.
Label whether a drawing is to scale.
Make force arrows begin on the specified object and distinguish force diagrams from motion arrows.
Use arrowheads for field directions and rays; use a normal where an angle depends on it.
Use consistent dots/crosses for out-of-page/into-page vectors and explain the convention.
Avoid crossed wires that look like junctions; mark electrical junctions unambiguously.
On spacetime diagrams use ct and x with equal physical scales for the unprimed light lines.
Make answer diagrams separate from question diagrams to avoid leaking a solution.
Provide mobile-readable labels and sufficient contrast without relying on colour alone.

qualityGate: Solve independently before writing distractors or the rubric.
Check dimensions, signs, limiting cases and physical magnitudes.
Recompute every numerical answer at full precision and only then round.
Verify all options are distinct after displayed rounding.
Check that the mark total equals the sum of subparts and marking-point caps.
Check the AHL tag against the corrected guide page, especially A.2 2D collisions and mixed topics.
Confirm that every required constant or uncommon relationship is supplied or legitimately available in the chosen data booklet.
Have a second pass explicitly look for ambiguous diagrams, unstated initial phase, reference-frame ambiguity, sign ambiguity, and hidden assumptions.
Do not claim official endorsement or reproduce question-bank material with changed numbers.

dataBookletVerification.confirmed: The official guide identifies the booklet as the source of circuit symbols, mathematical relationships, constants and course equations, with a clean copy used for every exam paper.
dataBookletVerification.notConfirmed: A public IB-hosted copy of the latest standalone booklet was not located in this primary-source-only research. Third-party copies and their asserted version numbers were not used.
dataBookletVerification.authoringAction: Use the corrected guide's equations and provide any essential constant in the independent item until the actual current school-provided booklet is checked. Link to official IB resources rather than bundling an unverified copy.

references.role: Corrected authoritative syllabus, boundaries and command terms
Verification that the corrected guide is the current examiner reference
Exam format and marking conventions only; no question adaptation
